hindi: “तुम और मैं शून्य को बसाते हैं” — यह अनवसित सन्धि है।
english: “Both you and I settle the empty [place]” — such is the anavasita treaty.
notes: anavasita kept as a term (glossary 3.16: literal sense in the gloss only). śūnyam is neuter, noun not stated; "[place]" is a supplied bracket (an empty land or settlement is meant by context). niveśayāvahe is 1st dual causative "we two cause to settle"; hortative "let us two settle" is possible. The quotation is closed by iti, which also opens the label.
lines_deva: "त्वं च-अहं च शून्यं निवेशयावहे" इत्य् अनवसित.सन्धिः
lines_iast: "tvaṃ ca-ahaṃ ca śūnyaṃ niveśayāvahe" ity anavasita.sandhiḥ

words.gloss: one whose purpose is at hand

hindi: उन दोनों में से जो प्रत्युपस्थित प्रयोजन वाला यथोक्त गुणों वाली भूमि को बसाता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: Of the two, he who, with his purpose at hand, settles land having the qualities as stated, outwits [the other].
notes: The object of atisandhatte is not stated; "[the other]" is a bracketed supply. pratyupasthita-artha: "whose purpose/gain is present (at hand)"; the alternative "who has a pressing need" is possible. "yathā-ukta-guṇām" refers back to the qualities of land stated earlier.
lines_deva: तयोर् यः प्रत्युपस्थित.अर्थो यथा.उक्त.गुणां भूमिं निवेशयति सो ऽतिसन्धत्ते
lines_iast: tayor yaḥ pratyupasthita.artho yathā.ukta.guṇāṃ bhūmiṃ niveśayati so 'tisandhatte

hindi: वहाँ भी “स्थल या जलीय” — बड़े स्थल से छोटा जलीय श्रेष्ठ, फलों की निरन्तरता और स्थिरता के कारण।
english: There too, “dry land or watery” — a small watery [one] [is] better than a large dry land, because of the continuity and the stability of the fruits.
notes: "sthalam audakaṃ vā iti" is a closed quotation with no opening mark (a question of choice, "dry land or watery?"); it is shown with quotation marks and iti is not rendered further (glossary 3.8). The same pattern recurs in units 18 and 23. "[one]" is a bracketed supply for the unnamed noun with audakam.
lines_deva: तत्र-अपि स्थलम् औदकं वा-इति महतः स्थलाद् अल्पम् औदकं श्रेयः, सातत्याद् अवस्थितत्वाच् च फलानाम्
lines_iast: tatra-api sthalam audakaṃ vā-iti mahataḥ sthalād alpam audakaṃ śreyaḥ, sātatyād avasthitatvāc ca phalānām

words.gloss: having abundant early and late crops

hindi: दो स्थलों में भी प्रचुर पूर्व और अपर सस्य वाला, अल्प वर्षा से पकने वाला, अबाध आरम्भ वाला श्रेष्ठ।
english: Even between two dry lands, [the one] having abundant early and late crops, ripening with little rain, [and] with unobstructed undertakings [is] better.
notes: varṣa may be "rain" or "year" (alpa-varṣa-pāka: ripening with little rain, or in a short time); the literal "rain" is taken. asakta: unattached/unobstructed. The noun with the neuter adjectives is not stated; "[the one]" is supplied. The three qualities have no ca between them; "and" is bracketed.
lines_deva: स्थलयोर् अपि प्रभूत.पूर्व.अपर.सस्यम् अल्प.वर्ष.पाकम् असक्त.आरम्भं श्रेयः
lines_iast: sthalayor api prabhūta.pūrva.apara.sasyam alpa.varṣa.pākam asakta.ārambhaṃ śreyaḥ

words.gloss: than one with sowing of non-grain

hindi: जलीय दोनों में भी धान्य की बुआई वाला अधान्य की बुआई वाले से श्रेष्ठ।
english: Even between two watery [lands], the one with the sowing of grain [is] better than the one with the sowing of non-grain.
notes: The e-text has "adhānya.vāpāt-śreyaḥ" with a "-" join of two words: adhānya-vāpāt and śreyaḥ. "lands" and "the one" are bracketed supplies; the noun is not stated.
lines_deva: औदकयोर् अपि धान्य.वापम् अधान्य.वापात्-श्रेयः
lines_iast: audakayor api dhānya.vāpam adhānya.vāpāt-śreyaḥ

hindi: उन दोनों की अल्पता और बहुलता में छोटे धान्य-कान्त से बड़ा अधान्य-कान्त श्रेष्ठ।
english: Of these two, in smallness and largeness, a large adhānya-kānta [is] better than a small dhānya-kānta.
notes: kānta is obscure here (literally "pleasing, beloved"); dhānya-kānta / adhānya-kānta are kept untranslated, no sense invented. Possible readings: a land "pleasing with grain" vs "not so", or kānta as a land-type. alpāt (printed alpān before mahad) and mahat are regular sandhi. alpa-bahutve is taken as a dvandva "smallness-and-largeness"; the dual alpa-bahutve is possible.
lines_deva: तयोर् अल्प.बहुत्वे धान्य.कान्ताद् अल्पान् महद् अधान्य.कान्तं श्रेयः
lines_iast: tayor alpa.bahutve dhānya.kāntād alpān mahad adhānya.kāntaṃ śreyaḥ

hindi: क्योंकि बड़े विस्तार में स्थाल्य और अनूप्य ओषधियाँ होती हैं।
english: For in a large expanse there are plants both sthālya and of marshy land.
notes: The e-text has "sthālyāś ca-anūpyāś ca-oṣadhayo": the "-" joins ca with the next word (ca anūpyāḥ; ca oṣadhayaḥ). sthālya is obscure (perhaps for sthalya "of dry land", cf. unit 3; or from sthālī "pot"); kept as printed, not flagged since the reading is uncertain. anūpya: from anūpa, marshy/watery land. oṣadhi: plants (herbs, crops).
lines_deva: महत्य् अवकाशे हि स्थाल्याश् च-अनूप्याश् च-ओषधयो भवन्ति
lines_iast: mahaty avakāśe hi sthālyāś ca-anūpyāś ca-oṣadhayo bhavanti

hindi: और दुर्ग आदि कर्म प्रचुरता से किए जाते हैं।
english: And the works beginning with the fort are done with abundance.

text_flags.why: possible: prabhūtya is not attested; prābhūtya = abundance (low certainty)

notes: prabhūtyena is taken as instrumental of prabhūtya "abundance" (abstract of prabhūta); possibly for prābhūtyena or prabhūtatvena; not flagged as the form is uncertain.
lines_deva: दुर्ग.आदीनि च कर्माणि प्रभूत्येन क्रियन्ते
lines_iast: durga.ādīni ca karmāṇi prabhūtyena kriyante

hindi: क्योंकि भूमि के गुण कृत्रिम हैं।
english: For the qualities of land [are] artificial.
notes: The printed "kṛtrimā hi" is regular sandhi for kṛtrimāḥ hi (āḥ before a voiced consonant becomes ā; glossary 7.10), not flagged. kṛtrima: made, artificial (brought about by effort).
lines_deva: कृत्रिमा हि भूमि.गुणाः
lines_iast: kṛtrimā hi bhūmi.guṇāḥ

words.gloss: of the enjoyment of mines and of grain

hindi: खनि और धान्य के भोग में खनि का भोग कोश बनाने वाला है; धान्य का भोग कोश, कोष्ठ, अगार बनाने वाला है।
english: Of the enjoyment of mines and the enjoyment of grain, the enjoyment of mines [is] the maker of the treasury; the enjoyment of grain [is] the maker of treasury, granary and storehouse.
notes: bhoga = enjoyment (literal, glossary 7.9; "use" of 3.8 left to a person). kara is taken as "maker/doer" (-kara agent suffix); the alternative "yielding a tax/revenue to X" is possible. In kośa-koṣṭha-agāra-kara the members may also be read as "kośa-koṣṭhāgāra" (treasury-granary) as one item; all three are given as members.
lines_deva: खनि.धान्य.भोगयोः खनि.भोगः कोश.करः, धान्य.भोगः कोश.कोष्ठ.अगार.करः
lines_iast: khani.dhānya.bhogayoḥ khani.bhogaḥ kośa.karaḥ, dhānya.bhogaḥ kośa.koṣṭha.agāra.karaḥ

hindi: क्योंकि दुर्ग आदि कर्मों के आरम्भ धान्य-मूल वाले हैं।
english: For the undertakings of the works beginning with forts have grain as their root.
notes: "dhānya.mūlā hi" is regular sandhi for dhānya-mūlāḥ hi (āḥ before a voiced consonant becomes ā; glossary 7.10), not flagged. karma = works (glossary 7.1).
lines_deva: धान्य.मूला हि दुर्ग.आदीनां कर्मणाम् आरम्भाः
lines_iast: dhānya.mūlā hi durga.ādīnāṃ karmaṇām ārambhāḥ

hindi: बड़े देश की बिक्री या खनि का भोग श्रेष्ठ।
english: The sale of a large territory, or the enjoyment of mines, [is] better.
notes: Literal reading with one "or" joining the two items; it may instead mean "or else the enjoyment of mines is better [than the sale of a large territory]". Both are noted, the literal one is rendered. viṣaya = territory (glossary 4.13).
lines_deva: महा.विषय.विक्रयो वा खनि.भोगः श्रेयान्
lines_iast: mahā.viṣaya.vikrayo vā khani.bhogaḥ śreyān

words.gloss: of the enjoyment of produce forests and elephant forests

hindi: “द्रव्य-वन और हस्ति-वन के भोग में द्रव्य-वन का भोग सब कर्मों का स्रोत है और प्रचुर संचय में समर्थ है; हस्ति-वन का भोग विपरीत है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: “Of the enjoyment of produce forests and of elephant forests, the enjoyment of a produce forest [is] the source of all works and [is] capable of abundant storing; the enjoyment of an elephant forest [is] the reverse,” say the teachers.
notes: dravya = produce (of forests); nidhāna = storing, depositing. The quotation opens at the start of the unit and iti closes it; ācāryāḥ = the teachers (glossary).
lines_deva: "द्रव्य.हस्ति.वन.भोगयोर् द्रव्य.वन.भोगः सर्व.कर्मणां योनिः प्रभूत.निधान.क्षमश् च, विपरीतो हस्ति.वन.भोगः" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "dravya.hasti.vana.bhogayor dravya.vana.bhogaḥ sarva.karmaṇāṃ yoniḥ prabhūta.nidhāna.kṣamaś ca, viparīto hasti.vana.bhogaḥ" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
notes: Formula na iti X, as in the glossary (12.1, 8.1).
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: अनेक द्रव्य-वन अनेक भूमियों में बुवाए जा सकते हैं; हस्ति-वन नहीं।
english: Many produce forests can be caused to be sown in many lands; not an elephant forest.
notes: anekam and anekasyām are singular ("many"/"manifold"); the rendering with plurals follows the sense; "a manifold produce forest in a manifold land" is the strict literal. vap = sow/plant. The reasoning of unit 16 follows.
lines_deva: शक्यं द्रव्य.वनम् अनेकम् अनेकस्यां भूमौ वापयितुम्, न हस्ति.वनम्
lines_iast: śakyaṃ dravya.vanam anekam anekasyāṃ bhūmau vāpayitum, na hasti.vanam

hindi: क्योंकि दूसरे के सेना-दल का वध हाथी-प्रधान है।
english: For the slaying of the other's division has elephants as its chief [means].
notes: The closing iti closes the reason begun in unit 15 (Kautilya's reply); it has no opening quotation and is not rendered. para = the other (glossary 9.2: not "enemy"). anīka = division (glossary 10.6). iti closes Kautilya's reason begun in unit 15 (after unit 14); compare glossary 3.8 (a closing iti with no opening quotation is carried by quotation marks); left unrendered here, a person should decide.
lines_deva: हस्ति.प्रधानो हि पर.अनीक.वध इति
lines_iast: hasti.pradhāno hi para.anīka.vadha iti

words.gloss: of the enjoyment of the water-route and of the land-route

hindi: जल-मार्ग और स्थल-मार्ग के भोग में जल-मार्ग का भोग अनित्य है; स्थल-मार्ग का भोग नित्य है।
english: Of the enjoyment of the water-route and the enjoyment of the land-route, the enjoyment of the water-route [is] impermanent; the enjoyment of the land-route [is] permanent.
lines_deva: वारि.स्थल.पथ.भोगयोर् अनित्यो वारि.पथ.भोगः, नित्यः स्थल.पथ.भोगः
lines_iast: vāri.sthala.patha.bhogayor anityo vāri.patha.bhogaḥ, nityaḥ sthala.patha.bhogaḥ

hindi: “भूमि टूटे हुए मनुष्यों वाली या श्रेणी के मनुष्यों वाली” — टूटे हुए मनुष्यों वाली श्रेष्ठ।
english: “Land having broken men, or having guild men” — [the one] having broken men [is] better.
notes: The quotation opens at the start of the unit (no marks in the e-text) and iti closes it (glossary 3.8). bhinna = broken (glossary 10.4/7.5); here probably "disunited, not organised into guilds"; the literal "broken" is kept. śreṇī = guild (cf. śreṇī-bala, guild troops).
lines_deva: भिन्न.मनुष्या श्रेणी.मनुष्या वा भूमिर् इति भिन्न.मनुष्या श्रेयसी
lines_iast: bhinna.manuṣyā śreṇī.manuṣyā vā bhūmir iti bhinna.manuṣyā śreyasī

hindi: टूटे हुए मनुष्यों वाली भोग्य होती है, और दूसरों के उपजाप के योग्य नहीं है, किन्तु आपत्ति सहने वाली नहीं है।
english: [Land] having broken men becomes fit to be used, and is not open to secret instigation by others, but [it is] not bearing adversity.
notes: The subject (bhūmiḥ, land) is understood from the feminine forms. anyeṣām is a genitive of the agent: "by others". anāpat.sahā: an-āpad-sahā, "not enduring adversity" (āpad = adversity, glossary 8.1). upajāpa = secret instigation (glossary 8.1).
lines_deva: भिन्न.मनुष्या भोग्या भवति, अनुपजाप्या च-अन्येषाम्, अनापत्.सहा तु
lines_iast: bhinna.manuṣyā bhogyā bhavati, anupajāpyā ca-anyeṣām, anāpat.sahā tu

hindi: श्रेणी के मनुष्यों वाली विपरीत है; कोप में बड़े दोषों वाली है।
english: [Land] having guild men [is] the reverse; in a revolt [it is] of great defects.
notes: kopa is taken as revolt (glossary 8.2); "anger" is possible. doṣa = defect (glossary 3.15). "viparītā": the reverse of unit 19 (not fit to be used, open to instigation, bears adversity) is the intended sense but is not stated, so no sense is added.
lines_deva: विपरीता श्रेणी.मनुष्या, कोपे महा.दोषा
lines_iast: viparītā śreṇī.manuṣyā, kope mahā.doṣā

words.gloss: in the settlement of the four varṇas
from the favour of stocks of wares and of loans

hindi: उसमें चातुर्वर्ण्य के निवेश में सब भोग सहने के कारण प्रायः निम्न वर्णों वाली श्रेष्ठ; खेती की बहुलता और स्थिरता के कारण किसानों वाली; खेती और अन्य आरम्भों की प्रेरक होने के कारण गो-रक्षकों वाली; पण्य के संचय और ऋण के अनुग्रह के कारण धनी वणिकों वाली।
english: In that [land], in the settlement of the four varṇas, [land] mostly of the lower varṇas [is] better, from bearing every enjoyment; [land] having cultivators [is better], from the abundance and stability of agriculture; [land] having cow-keepers [is better], from being the promoter both of agriculture and of other undertakings; [land] having rich merchants [is better], from the favour of stocks of wares and of loans.
notes: Three clauses lack a verb; śreyasī is carried over (bracketed in English only). kṛṣyāḥ is genitive of kṛṣi (agriculture). prayojaka: one who sets in motion/promotes; "employer" is possible. paṇya-nicaya-ṛṇa-anugraha: the exact grouping (favour of stocks and loans / favour by way of stocks, loans) is uncertain; members given literally. The two ca…ca before ārambhāṇām are rendered "both … and" (glossary 7.5). avara = lower.
lines_deva: तस्यां चातुर्वर्ण्य.निवेशे सर्व.भोग.सहत्वाद् अवर.वर्ण.प्राया श्रेयसी, बाहुल्याद् ध्रुवत्वाच् च कृष्याः कर्षकवती, कृष्याश् च-अन्येषां च-आरम्भाणां प्रयोजकत्वात् गो.रक्षकवती, पण्य.निचय.ऋण.अनुग्रहाद् आढ्य.वणिग्वती
lines_iast: tasyāṃ cāturvarṇya.niveśe sarva.bhoga.sahatvād avara.varṇa.prāyā śreyasī, bāhulyād dhruvatvāc ca kṛṣyāḥ karṣakavatī, kṛṣyāś ca-anyeṣāṃ ca-ārambhāṇāṃ prayojakatvāt go.rakṣakavatī, paṇya.nicaya.ṛṇa.anugrahād āḍhya.vaṇigvatī

hindi: भूमि के गुणों में आश्रय श्रेष्ठ।
english: Of the qualities of land, the refuge [is] better.
notes: apāśraya (apa-āśraya) = support, refuge, what one leans on; the following unit compares land supported by forts with land supported by men. The sentence may also mean "support is the better of the qualities of land". Rendered "refuge" (glossary 7.12).
lines_deva: भूमि.गुणानाम् अपाश्रयः श्रेयान्
lines_iast: bhūmi.guṇānām apāśrayaḥ śreyān

hindi: “भूमि दुर्ग के आश्रय वाली या पुरुषों के आश्रय वाली” — पुरुषों के आश्रय वाली श्रेष्ठ।
english: “Land having the fort as its refuge, or having men as its refuge” — [the one] having men as its refuge [is] better.
notes: Quotation opens at the start of the unit and iti closes it, as unit 18. puruṣa = man (men); "people" is possible.
lines_deva: दुर्ग.अपाश्रया पुरुष.अपाश्रया वा भूमिर् इति पुरुष.अपाश्रया श्रेयसी
lines_iast: durga.apāśrayā puruṣa.apāśrayā vā bhūmir iti puruṣa.apāśrayā śreyasī

hindi: क्योंकि राज्य पुरुषों वाला है।
english: For a kingdom [is] possessing men.
notes: puruṣavat may be possessive "having men" (taken here, the sense of unit 25) or comparative "like a man" (a kingdom is like a man). "puruṣavad dhi" is regular sandhi (t + h becomes d dh), not flagged.
lines_deva: पुरुषवद् धि राज्यम्
lines_iast: puruṣavad dhi rājyam

hindi: पुरुष-रहित गाय बाँझ ही है; क्या दुहे?
english: A cow without a man [is] barren indeed; what would [one] milk?

text_flags.why: possible: vandhyā + eva would give vandhyaiva; vandhy eva suggests a stem in -i/-ī; read vandhyā eva by sense

notes: Proverb-like: a cow without a man (a herdsman) gives nothing. The subject of duhīta is unstated ("[one]"). apuruṣā could also be "without men".
lines_deva: अपुरुषा गौर् वन्ध्य् एव किं दुहीत
lines_iast: apuruṣā gaur vandhy eva kiṃ duhīta

words.gloss: having great loss and expenditure in its settlement

hindi: किन्तु महान् क्षय और व्यय वाली बसावट की भूमि को पाने की इच्छा वाला पहले ही दुर्बल, राज-बीज से रहित, उत्साहहीन, पक्षहीन, अन्यायपूर्ण आचरण वाले, व्यसन वाले, दैव को प्रमाण मानने वाले अथवा जो कुछ करने वाले क्रेता से सौदा करे।
english: But one desiring to obtain land whose settlement involves great loss and expenditure should first indeed strike a bargain with a buyer [who is] weak, not of royal seed, without energy, without a party, of unjust conduct, given to vice (vyasana), taking the divine as authority, or doing anything whatever.
notes: paṇ = strike a bargain (glossary 7.7). arāja-bījin: bījin = "of seed/descent", so "not of royal descent"; kept literal. vyasanin: "given to vice" (glossary 4.6; personal faults 7.6, 8.3); "afflicted" (3.11, exception list) is possible. daiva-pramāṇa: "taking fate/the divine as the authority". kṣaya = loss, vyaya = expenditure (glossary 9.4). The list of adjectives has only the final vā.
lines_deva: महा.क्षय.व्यय.निवेशां तु भूमिम् अवाप्तु.कामः पूर्वम् एव क्रेतारं पणेत दुर्बलम् अराज.बीजिनं निरुत्साहम् अपक्षम् अन्याय.वृत्तिं व्यसनिनं दैव.प्रमाणं यत्.किञ्चन.कारिणं वा
lines_iast: mahā.kṣaya.vyaya.niveśāṃ tu bhūmim avāptu.kāmaḥ pūrvam eva kretāraṃ paṇeta durbalam arāja.bījinaṃ nirutsāham apakṣam anyāya.vṛttiṃ vyasaninaṃ daiva.pramāṇaṃ yat.kiñcana.kāriṇaṃ vā

words.gloss: having great loss and expenditure in its settlement

hindi: क्योंकि महान् क्षय और व्यय वाली बसावट की भूमि में बसा हुआ दुर्बल राज-बीज वाला सगन्ध प्रकृतियों के साथ क्षय और व्यय से डूबता है।
english: For in land whose settlement involves great loss and expenditure, a weak one of royal seed, having settled, sinks down together with [his] constituent elements of the same smell (sagandha) through loss and expenditure.
notes: sagandha ("of the same smell") is obscure; it is kept literal (probably "of like kind", i.e. kinsmen/neighbouring), with asagandha in unit 28 as its opposite. The e-text joins kṣaya.vyayena-avasīdati with "-": two words, kṣaya-vyayena and avasīdati. prakṛti = constituent elements (glossary).
lines_deva: महा.क्षय.व्यय.निवेशायां हि भूमौ दुर्बलो राज.बीजी निविष्टः सगन्धाभिः प्रकृतिभिः सह क्षय.व्ययेन-अवसीदति
lines_iast: mahā.kṣaya.vyaya.niveśāyāṃ hi bhūmau durbalo rāja.bījī niviṣṭaḥ sagandhābhiḥ prakṛtibhiḥ saha kṣaya.vyayena-avasīdati

words.gloss: from fear of loss and expenditure

hindi: बलवान् राज-बीज से रहित क्षय और व्यय के भय से असगन्ध प्रकृतियों द्वारा त्याग दिया जाता है।
english: A strong one not of royal seed is abandoned by [his] constituent elements not of the same smell (asagandha), from fear of loss and expenditure.
notes: asagandha is the opposite of sagandha (unit 27), kept literal. The e-text prints "prakṛtibhis tyajyate" (s before t, regular visarga sandhi).
lines_deva: बलवान् अराज.बीजी क्षय.व्यय.भयाद् असगन्धाभिः प्रकृतिभिस् त्यज्यते
lines_iast: balavān arāja.bījī kṣaya.vyaya.bhayād asagandhābhiḥ prakṛtibhis tyajyate

hindi: किन्तु उत्साहहीन, सेना वाला होते हुए भी, सेना का प्रणेता न होने वाला, सेना सहित क्षय और व्यय से टूट जाता है।
english: But one without energy, even though having an army, [being] a non-leader of the army, is broken together with his army by loss and expenditure.
notes: daṇḍa = army here (Book 7 convention). praṇetṛ: leader, one who directs; "one who does not apply/use the army" is possible. avabhajyate is read as the passive of √bhañj (is broken); a passive of √bhaj ("is divided") is the alternative.
lines_deva: निरुत्साहस् तु दण्डवान् अपि दण्डस्य-अप्रणेता सदण्डः क्षय.व्ययेन-अवभज्यते
lines_iast: nirutsāhas tu daṇḍavān api daṇḍasya-apraṇetā sadaṇḍaḥ kṣaya.vyayena-avabhajyate

words.gloss: from lacking favour in loss and expenditure

hindi: कोश वाला भी, पक्षहीन, क्षय और व्यय में अनुग्रह से रहित होने के कारण, कहीं से प्राप्त नहीं करता।
english: Even one having a treasury, [being] without a party, from lacking favour in loss and expenditure, obtains [it] from nowhere.
notes: The object of prāpnoti (the land) is not stated; "[it]" is a bracketed supply. anugraha = favour (glossary 7.8). The compound kṣaya-vyaya-anugraha could be "favour regarding loss and expenditure" or "favour in the matter of losses and expenses"; literal given.
lines_deva: कोशवान् अप्य् अपक्षः क्षय.व्यय.अनुग्रह.हीनत्वान् न कुतश्चित् प्राप्नोति
lines_iast: kośavān apy apakṣaḥ kṣaya.vyaya.anugraha.hīnatvān na kutaścit prāpnoti

hindi: अन्यायपूर्ण आचरण वाला बसे हुए को भी उठवाए।
english: One of unjust conduct would cause even [one] who is settled to rise up.
notes: utthāpayet is the causative "make rise up", here by sense "dislodge, evict"; kept literal. The person meant is the buyer of unit 26.
lines_deva: अन्याय.वृत्तिर् निविष्टम् अप्य् उत्थापयेत्
lines_iast: anyāya.vṛttir niviṣṭam apy utthāpayet

hindi: वह बिना बसे हुए को कैसे बसाए?
english: How would he settle [one] not settled?
notes: Meaning: one who dislodges the settled would not settle the unsettled (i.e. he will not populate waste land). The object of niveśayet is not stated ("[one]").
lines_deva: स कथम् अनिविष्टं निवेशयेत्
lines_iast: sa katham aniviṣṭaṃ niveśayet

hindi: इससे व्यसन वाले की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, the one given to vice is explained.
notes: Formula "tena X vyākhyātaḥ" (glossary 4.1). vyasanin refers back to the buyer in unit 26.
lines_deva: तेन व्यसनी व्याख्यातः
lines_iast: tena vyasanī vyākhyātaḥ

words.gloss: one whose undertaking of works has failed

hindi: दैव को प्रमाण मानने वाला, मानुष से हीन, आरम्भ से रहित अथवा जिसके कर्मों का आरम्भ विफल हुआ, डूबता है।
english: One taking the divine as authority, deprived of mānuṣa, without undertaking, or one whose undertaking of works has failed, sinks down.
notes: mānuṣa is kept untranslated (glossary 3.6: not the 6.2 "the human"); the sense "human effort" is the evident contrast with daiva, mentioned here only. vipanna = failed, gone wrong. The e-text joins vā-avasīdati with "-": two words.
lines_deva: दैव.प्रमाणो मानुष.हीनो निरारम्भो विपन्न.कर्म.आरम्भो वा-अवसीदति
lines_iast: daiva.pramāṇo mānuṣa.hīno nirārambho vipanna.karma.ārambho vā-avasīdati

hindi: जो कुछ करने वाला कुछ प्राप्त नहीं करता।
english: One doing anything whatever obtains nothing.
notes: āsādayati (caus. of ā-√sad) = brings about, reaches, obtains; "finds" is possible.
lines_deva: यत्.किञ्चन.कारी न किञ्चिद् आसादयति
lines_iast: yat.kiñcana.kārī na kiñcid āsādayati

hindi: और वह इनमें सबसे बुरा होता है।
english: And he becomes the worst of these.
notes: pāpiṣṭhatama: pāpa "bad, evil" with a double superlative; "worst, most evil". The e-text joins ca-eṣām with "-": two words. "He" is sa.
lines_deva: स च-एषां पापिष्ठतमो भवति
lines_iast: sa ca-eṣāṃ pāpiṣṭhatamo bhavati

hindi: “क्योंकि जो कुछ आरम्भ करने वाला विजिगीषु का कभी छिद्र पा सकता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: “For one undertaking anything whatever may at some time find a weak point of the conqueror,” say the teachers.
notes: vijigīṣu = the conqueror (glossary 6.2); chidra = weak point (glossary 13.4). The quotation opens at the start of the unit.
lines_deva: "यत्.किञ्चिद्.आरभमाणो हि विजिगीषोः कदाचिच् छिद्रम् आसादयेद्" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: "yat.kiñcid.ārabhamāṇo hi vijigīṣoḥ kadācic chidram āsādayed" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “जैसे छिद्र, वैसे विनाश भी पा सकता है,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “As [he may find] a weak point, so [he] may find even destruction,” says Kautilya.
notes: Reply to unit 37; the subject (the undertaker of anything whatever) is unstated, "[he]" is bracketed. Formula "... iti X" (glossary 3.5).
lines_deva: यथा छिद्रं तथा विनाशम् अप्य् आसादयेद् इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: yathā chidraṃ tathā vināśam apy āsādayed iti kauṭilyaḥ

words.gloss: in the support of the heel-seizer

hindi: उनकी अप्राप्ति में, जैसे पार्ष्णिग्राह के सहारे के विषय में कहेंगे, वैसे भूमि को स्थापित करे।
english: In the non-obtaining of them, as we shall state in the support (upagraha) of the heel-seizer, so [he] should establish the land.
notes: teṣām refers to the buyers of unit 26. pārṣṇi-grāha = the heel-seizer (glossary 6.2); upagraha = support (glossary 7.8). Whether the support is given to the heel-seizer or by him is not stated; it points to a later passage. alābha = non-obtaining (glossary 7.10). avasthāpayet: "should establish/set up", also "should arrange"; the object (the land) and the subject are as printed.
lines_deva: तेषाम् अलाभे यथा पार्ष्णि.ग्राह.उपग्रहे वक्ष्यामस् तथा भूमिम् अवस्थापयेत्
lines_iast: teṣām alābhe yathā pārṣṇi.grāha.upagrahe vakṣyāmas tathā bhūmim avasthāpayet

hindi: यह अभिहित सन्धि है।
english: Such is the abhihita treaty.
notes: Closing label (glossary 3.9/5.2). abhihita ("stated, declared") is kept as a term; sandhi = treaty as a named kind (glossary 7.3).
lines_deva: इत्य् अभिहित.सन्धिः
lines_iast: ity abhihita.sandhiḥ

hindi: गुणवती अथवा आदेय भूमि के लिए बलवान् द्वारा क्रय से माँगा गया, सन्धि स्थापित करके दे।
english: Asked by a strong one, by purchase, for land possessing qualities or acceptable, [he] should give [it], having established peace.
notes: Subject unstated ("[he]"), the owner of the land. ādeya = acceptable (glossary 9.4). krayeṇa: "by purchase / as a purchase". bare sandhi = peace (glossary 7.3); "treaty" is possible here, a person should decide.
lines_deva: गुणवतीम् आदेयां वा भूमिं बलवता क्रयेण याचितः सन्धिम् अवस्थाप्य दद्यात्
lines_iast: guṇavatīm ādeyāṃ vā bhūmiṃ balavatā krayeṇa yācitaḥ sandhim avasthāpya dadyāt

hindi: यह अनिभृत सन्धि है।
english: Such is the anibhṛta treaty.
notes: Closing label. anibhṛta is kept as a term; the literal sense "not hidden / not steady / not modest" is uncertain.
lines_deva: इत्य् अनिभृत.सन्धिः
lines_iast: ity anibhṛta.sandhiḥ

words.gloss: gain of an ally and money

hindi: अथवा बराबर वाले द्वारा माँगा गया, कारण पर विचार करके दे — “मेरे द्वारा भूमि प्रत्यादेय है अथवा वश में है; इससे बँधा हुआ दूसरा मेरे वश में होगा; अथवा भूमि की बिक्री से मित्र और धन का लाभ मेरे लिए कार्य की सामर्थ्य करने वाला होगा।”
english: Or, asked by an equal, having considered the reason, [he] should give — “The land is retakable by me, or under control; another, bound by this, will come under my control; or, from the sale of land, the gain of an ally and money, producing capability for the task, will be mine.”

text_flags.why: possible: stray hyphen glued to the word; it marks a dash/clause break inside the quotation, not a join with the next word

notes: The thought of the giver is quoted; iti closes it and is carried by the quotation marks. "[he]" is the unstated subject (the owner). pratyādeya = retakable (glossary 9.4). kārya-sāmarthya-kara: "making capability for the task" (kārya = task, matter). The hyphen in "bhaviṣyati-" is read as a dash, punctuation only. me in pratyādeyā me bhūmiḥ may be genitive "my land" or instrumental "by me".
lines_deva: समेन वा याचितः कारणम् अवेक्ष्य दद्यात् "प्रत्यादेया मे भूमिर् वश्या वा, अनया प्रतिबद्धः परो मे वश्यो भविष्यति- भूमि.विक्रयाद् वा मित्र.हिरण्य.लाभः कार्य.सामर्थ्य.करो मे भविष्यति" इति
lines_iast: samena vā yācitaḥ kāraṇam avekṣya dadyāt "pratyādeyā me bhūmir vaśyā vā, anayā pratibaddhaḥ paro me vaśyo bhaviṣyati- bhūmi.vikrayād vā mitra.hiraṇya.lābhaḥ kārya.sāmarthya.karo me bhaviṣyati" iti

hindi: इससे हीन क्रेता की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, the inferior buyer is explained.
notes: Formula "tena X vyākhyātaḥ" (glossary 4.1). hīna = the inferior (glossary 7.5), here taken with kretā; "the buyer who is inferior" is the sense: the unit extends units 41-43 to the case where the buyer is weaker.
lines_deva: तेन हीनः क्रेता व्याख्यातः
lines_iast: tena hīnaḥ kretā vyākhyātaḥ

hindi: इस प्रकार मित्र और धन को, जन-सहित और जन-रहित भूमि को पाता हुआ शास्त्र का ज्ञाता सामवायिकों को छल लेता है।
english: In this way, obtaining an ally and money, land with people and without people, the knower of the treatise outwits the associates.
notes: gām = earth, land (acc. of go). sajanām ajanām ca: "with people and without people". hiraṇya = money (glossary 5.2). sāmavāyika = associate (glossary 7.5), kept as a term. śāstra-vit: one who knows the treatise (śāstra). Two lines of an anuṣṭubh verse.
lines_deva: एवं मित्रं हिरण्यं च सजनाम् अजनां च गाम्
लभमानो ऽतिसन्धत्ते शास्त्रवित् सामवायिकान्
lines_iast: evaṃ mitraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca sajanām ajanāṃ ca gām
labhamāno 'tisandhatte śāstravit sāmavāyikān
